findings.title: A device that pushes while it still counts the old time keeper gets the join's layout but not its 'joined' result, so it shows 'No match' after NO_MATCH_AFTER
findings.why: The fix keeps early layouts from the next time keeper but not its join results. In the window #61 is about (C still counts A as time keeper), C's push is matched by B, B's 'joined' is dropped by fromLeader at C, and C's own wait times out and emits nomatch with timedOut and latest true. index.html then toasts 'No match. Tap again together' on C, even though C now holds B's layout with the B-C join. The new four-device two-browser step pushes in exactly this window but only checks joins, not C's toast. This was already true before the change and the ticket's acceptance only covers the layout, so it's Low.

findings.title: A forged layout under the next time keeper's id is now taken up at hand-over without asking
findings.why: earlyLayouts keeps a layout from any device in the room under whatever `from` it claims. Just before the time keeper leaves, a stranger can send {from: <next in line>, joins: ...}. When the hand-over happens, electLeader uses it, and because something usable was kept it skips the layoutask that would have fetched the real layout. That lasts until the new time keeper sends its layout again. Forging `from` for the current time keeper already works (known, #24), so this doesn't open a new kind of attack, but it touches T-S5, which the ticket names.
